problem:
The fifth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=-2$ is given by

$$
{P}_{5}(x)=-3+5(x+2)-7(x+2)^{2}+9(x+2)^{3}-11(x+2)^{4}+13(x+2)^{5}.
$$

What is ${f}^{(5)}(-2)?$

The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=3+\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{9}{5}{x}^{2}-4{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{″}(0)?$

feedback.worked_solution:
The coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{″}(0)}{2!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(0)}{2!} & =\frac{9}{5} \\ \frac{{f}^{″}(0)}{2} & =\frac{9}{5} \\ {f}^{″}(0) & =\frac{18}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
